paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God is great and God is close, and David sings about both in the same breath. David says God has exalted His name and His word "above all else" (Psalm 138:2). And yet "Though the LORD is on high, He attends to the lowly" (Psalm 138:6). The One who is above everything is paying attention to the little ones. I know a few things about being little, and I'm still amazed.

That's why David can give thanks with ALL his heart (Psalm 138:1). He isn't thanking a God who is far off or a God who forgets. He remembers a day when he called and God answered, and God "emboldened" him and "strengthened" his soul (Psalm 138:3). So when you're thankful, baker, look back at the times God has answered you. Gratitude gets a lot easier to give when you remember what He's done.

And look how far David's confidence reaches. He knows God will preserve him even in the midst of trouble (Psalm 138:7), and he says, "The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me" (Psalm 138:8). Then he prays, "do not abandon the works of Your hands" (Psalm 138:8). He is leaning on the God whose "loving devotion endures forever," not on his own strength. You are the work of His hands too, friend, so you can walk through your trouble thankful, because He isn't done with you.
